question: Recent cases involving EU-based organisations and financial institutions, including Banca Etica’s suspension of banking services to Autistici/Inventati following a US sanctions designation, have highlighted the potential impact of restrictive measures by non-EU countries on financial services within the single market.

The June 2026 Risk Assessment Report of the European Banking Authority (EBA) identifies substantial dependencies on information and communication technology and payment service providers that are not part of the European Economic Area.

While existing EBA guidelines address unwarranted de-risking arising from anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism considerations, their applicability to decisions driven by exposure to non-EU country sanctions remains unclear.
These developments raise questions concerning the prudential management of sanctionsrelated risks, proportional access to financial services and the EU’s operational and regulatory autonomy. 1.

Has the Commission assessed or collected data on banking restrictions resulting from non-EU country sanctions not incorporated into EU law, particularly those affecting organisations and legal entities and their access to essential financial services within the single market?

What supervisory safeguards and proportionality requirements apply when EU banks restrict lawful services due to exposure to non-EU country sanctions, particularly for legal entities not protected under the Payment Accounts Directive?

Following the Commission notice to EU operators of 23 October 2026 concerning the International Criminal Court, does the Commission envisage further guidance or supervisory measures to protect other EU operators from similar banking disruptions?
